- Look for an emphasis on addressing a “massive problem” at the border with Mexico.
- Look for support for a colleague’s amendment and continued cooperation to solve the border issue.

text: Is the Senator under the impression that some of the State commissions would not be willing. under proper persuasion. to vote to let the telephone companies raise rates from 10 to 15 cents on local calls and higher on longdistance rates. if necessary. in order to permit American Telephone & Telegraph Co. to finance itself?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward higher local telephone rates as a way to finance a private corporation, like 'raise rates', 'finance itself'.
- Look for concern about long-distance charges increasing alongside local call prices, like 'higher on longdistance rates'.
- Look for scrutiny of state commissions’ independence when facing pressure to approve rate increases, like 'under proper persuasion'.

text: If the leader will yield. I think there is considerable sentiment on my side of the aisle to act on the final measure. the Members tax situation. and act on a voice vote. sustain the position of the Senate. and send it back and do it tonight. but I understand there may be problems with other Senators.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for willingness to act on a tax measure quickly, including “do it tonight”.
- Look for support for a voice vote and sustaining the Senate’s position.
- Look for attention to Members’ tax situations as a reason to move the measure.

text: There are not enough hours left in the weeks between now and January 10 for them to do this work and do their business. If they did nothing but sit down and figure and fill out this form. they would not have the time to do it. The chain stores can. but not the independent retailer.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that compliance burdens overwhelm small independent businesses compared with large chains like 'The chain stores can', 'not the independent retailer'.
- Look for skepticism toward government paperwork requirements that consume small businesses’ limited time, as in 'fill out this form'.

text: Mr. Chairman. in view of the recent statement of an explanation of the gentleman from Alabama as to the competitive principle in this tariff. I would like to ask the gentleman whether on the paragraph we passed a short time ago. as to automobiles. the 45 per cent Is a competitive or a revenueraising rate?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for questioning whether an automobile tariff rate is designed for competition or revenue collection.
- Look for attention to tariff policy and the economic effects of duties on automobiles.
- Look for scrutiny of how tariff rates are justified under a competitive principle.

text: Under the legislation. a mother of a child of 6 months. 1 year. 2 years. 3 years. or 4 years can be made to leave the home and work somewhere. in some area. for perhaps 25 or 30 cents an hour. going into a courthouse and cleaning the latrine there. or doing any kind of labor.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that mothers of very young children may be forced to leave home for work.
- Look for criticism of compelled labor under legislation.
- Look for attention to exploitative wages like '25 or 30 cents an hour'.
- Look for concern about people being assigned degrading work like 'cleaning the latrine'.

text: I do not mean to question that the Senator would keep his word. but may I say that when he attempts to bring down the prices of agricultural products. he will find about 2.000.000 of the angriest farmers he ever saw right outside the doors here who will want to know why their prosperity Is being taken away from them.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that lowering agricultural prices would threaten farmers’ prosperity.
- Look for attention to farmers as a distinct constituency with a strong stake in policy.
- Look for rhetorical emphasis on farmers’ anger if their economic well-being is undermined.

text: Mr. Chairman. I yield myself such time as I may consume. Mr. Chairman. I conclude by just saying this is not about cutting the NEA. This is continuing the level of funding and moving the money that we increased to energy conservation. a priority between energy conservation and increasing the NEA.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for prioritizing energy conservation over increased arts funding.
- Look for framing the choice as redirecting money toward a policy priority rather than cutting funding.
- Look for support for maintaining existing funding levels while opposing an increase.

text: Yes. sir. a request to insert these tables and communications in the RECORD for the information of Senators. andparticularly of the members of the Appropriations Committee and the Efficiency Board. These salaries ought to be equalized. There ought to be a readjustment of salaries throughout the country everywhere. there is no doubt .about that An my mind.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for advocating equal pay across comparable positions, as in 'These salaries ought to be equalized'.
- Look for support for broad salary adjustments across the country, as in 'throughout the country everywhere'.

text: In my district I am taking care of the farmers by having men on the W. P. A. leave the W. P. A. under the condition that if they do not they will not be continued on the W. P. A. rolls. also. by having the commissioner of education defer entrance to college in the fall.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern for local farmers and agricultural livelihoods.
- Look for using public works jobs to address local needs like 'taking care of the farmers'.
- Look for pressure on workers to leave public assistance employment or risk losing benefits like 'not be continued on the W. P. A. rolls'.
- Look for adjusting college entry to manage local public employment needs like 'defer entrance to college'.

text: I have. We have a bill on the calendar now. It is not reported yet. but it is authorized to be reported. The gentleman from Illinois . of the Public Lands Committee. has been designated to write the report. It Was introduced by me. It has the support of the conservativepeople of this country.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for a claim of support from conservative people as a signal of cross-ideological appeal like 'conservativepeople'.
- Look for emphasis on a bill’s procedural status and committee process, rather than a detailed policy argument, like 'authorized to be reported'.
- Look for personal ownership of legislation as a way to frame the speaker’s role like 'introduced by me'.

text: Then. if we need that program. consistent with other transportation needs of the country. why does not my colleague from Illinois want to allow this program to continue until the interstate system is completed? I will dispute the figures. We are going to have a deficit before the job is actually done.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for continuing a transportation program until the interstate system is completed.
- Look for prioritizing consistency between transportation spending and “other transportation needs of the country”.
- Look for concern that the program may end before the job is finished, as in “until the interstate system is completed”.
- Look for questioning a colleague’s opposition to keeping a public infrastructure program in place.

text: Mr. Speaker. reserving the right to object. this seems to be one of these habitual conferences in which we are continuously participating over in some foreign country. Although its purpose may be perfectly laudable. I cannot yet say whether it is or not. I wish the gentleman from New York would explain the purpose of the joint resolution.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward recurring participation in conferences held in foreign countries.
- Look for requesting a clear explanation of a joint resolution’s purpose before endorsing it.
- Look for withholding judgment on a proposal while acknowledging that its purpose may be laudable.

text: I know of cases in which I am interested that have dragged along for months. and every time I call attention to them they say that they are limited in the amount of money. and it seems to me that it is impossible for them to carry out the purposes for which the commission was created.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for criticism that a commission lacks sufficient funding to fulfill its mission.
- Look for concern that cases have dragged on for months.
- Look for constituent advocacy through personal follow-up, like 'I call attention to them'.

text: The bottom line. I say to the Senator. is that if we want to get something done. we really cant afford to wait. There are so many slips between the cup and the lip. especially on an issue such as this. that we ought to be moving and not waiting 2 weeks but appointing conferees tomorrow.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for urgency in advancing legislation and skepticism about delaying action.
- Look for a call to appoint conferees immediately like 'appointing conferees tomorrow'.

text: The gentleman spoke of our standing behind these people who are holding the front lines. How can the gentleman be sure they will stay in front of us and not shift their positior. and put us in front Cf them? The gist of the arguments here today has been that the British are not doing the job.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that allies may shift their position and leave U.S. forces exposed, like 'put us in front'
- Look for skepticism toward claims that the British are failing to meet their responsibilities, like 'not doing the job'
- Look for emphasis on protecting those holding the front lines, like 'holding the front lines'

text: Mr. Speaker. the purpose of H.R. 10874 is to establish a new national seashore on the Gulf of Mexico. to be known as the Gulf Islands National Seashore. It will be a prime recreation area for a sevenState regionMississippi. Florida. Louisiana. Alabama. Georgia. Arkansas. and Tennesseewhere some 23 million people reside. The Department of Interior favors the bill.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for federal designation and protection of a major recreation area through a national seashore.
- Look for emphasis on broad regional benefits, citing residents across seven states.
- Look for alignment with the Interior Department’s position on the proposed bill.

text: The gentleman from Michigan is indeed proceeding in order. He is proceeding in order of the needs and the will of 40 million Americans who are concerned about Medicare. He is proceeding in order to take care of the needs of the people in this country who depend upon Medicaid.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for prioritizing Medicare and the concerns of the people who rely on it.
- Look for support for Medicaid as a program that meets people’s needs.
- Look for framing health care policy around the needs and will of ordinary Americans.

text: In view of the fact that less than onethird of our virgin timber remains. and in view further of the fact that in oe State. my own. we lose more in dollars than this whole bill provides. does not the gentleman think it is about time we did something to prevent fire alone. eliminating all of the other provisions?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for government action to prevent destructive fires.
- Look for concern about conserving the remaining virgin timber.
- Look for emphasis on the economic losses caused by fires, like 'we lose more in dollars'.
- Look for advocating action even if it means eliminating other provisions, like 'prevent fire alone'.

text: Is it not also a fact that under the terms of this bill. section 616 to be exact. the President has the authority at any time he deems such action to be necessary in the interest of national defense to waive the socalled antidefIciency law and to spend the money available as rapidly as he sees fit?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that the president could spend funds rapidly at his discretion.
- Look for skepticism toward executive authority to waive limits on government spending.
- Look for emphasis on national defense as a justification for presidential spending powers.

text: I simply wanted at this point to say that I do not know that I have been approached by any lobbyist. to know him. but you now want to tag all my friends as lobbyists who come here from my State. You want to tag them as such. and I object.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to labeling people as lobbyists without clear grounds, like 'I object'.
- Look for concern that visitors from the speaker’s state are being unfairly categorized, like 'my friends', 'my State'.
- Look for a defensive framing that challenges accusations of lobbying, like 'I do not know'.

text: Mr. Chairman. the PostmasterGeneral finds that this act that we have recently passed. which goes into effect on the 1st of May. turns the postal revenues of Porto Rico into the public Treasury. and that he would have no means of running the postal service in Porto Rico without a deficiency appropriation.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that a government policy redirects postal revenues into the public Treasury.
- Look for opposition to operating a public service through a “deficiency appropriation”.
- Look for emphasis on whether the postal service can cover its own costs from its revenues.

text: I would like to ask the gentleman a question. Has not the Department ruled the Kreutzer Sonata out of the mails. and is not all matter like that. which is probably indecent and obscene literature. ruled out? Why can not the gentleman get all of this. stuff ruled out of the mails in that way?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for excluding literature deemed indecent or obscene from the postal system, like 'ruled out of the mails'.
- Look for framing censorship as a way to keep allegedly obscene material from circulating, like 'indecent and obscene literature'.

text: I refer to agencies created under the war powers. The Senator is correct. there are about 14 agencies relating to housing. and only 7 of these are dealt with In this plan. Not a single one of them is abolished. There would still be six or seven additional agencies dealing with housing which are not covered by the plan.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern about fragmented federal housing administration across multiple agencies.
- Look for emphasis on the plan leaving existing housing agencies intact, like 'Not a single one of them is abolished'.
- Look for attention to housing agencies excluded from the plan, like 'not covered by the plan'.

text: I am curious as to why the distinguished chairman of the committee did not touch on the international features of the bill. One of the aspects of the House bill that gave me the most trouble was the taxation of foreign subsidiaries. Was the gentleman going to cover that point?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern about how tax legislation affects foreign subsidiaries.
- Look for scrutiny of the bill’s international tax provisions like 'international features'.
- Look for questioning committee leadership about omitted policy details like 'did not touch on'.

text: Mr. Chairman. on rollcall No. 20. I inadvertently cast an "aye" vote when my vote should have been "no" in opposition to the Ney substitute to H.R. 2356. The Ney substitute would undermine the ability of Legal Permanent Residents to participate in the political system. I ask that the RECORD reflect my opposition to the Ney substitute.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for defending the political participation of immigrants with permanent legal status.
- Look for opposing legislative changes described as undermining residents’ ability to participate in the political system.

text: Whereas. if the Dingell amendment were to be passed. EPA would act most wisely. If. in fact. the assumptions are analyzed. it is just as possible to argue that the Dingell amendment would result in a 10percent fuel economy loss in 1982 relative to the committee bill. It just depends on ones assumptions.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward the amendment’s projected fuel-economy effects, noting that different assumptions could yield a 10 percent loss.
- Look for emphasis on analyzing assumptions before accepting claims about policy outcomes.
- Look for comparison of the amendment with the committee bill as a basis for evaluating fuel-economy impacts.

text: I would agree. I want to ask my friend this question: Would you suggest we could eliminate from the Federal court the power to use the remedy of injunction to enforce the first amendment. leaving to the perFebrutart.1.1982 sons who are injured a damage remedy? Would you call that enforcing an amendment?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for defending the First Amendment by questioning whether removing courts’ power to issue injunctions would adequately enforce it.
- Look for concern that people harmed by constitutional violations should have an effective remedy.
- Look for framing access to judicial relief as essential to protecting individual rights.

text: Will this procedure under suspension of the rules also make in order matters which would normally be subject to the jurisdiction of the Committee on Ways and Meansin other words. you have no way of challenging a point of order against the housing bill which incorporates a great tax advantage for the rich?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for criticism of tax advantages perceived to benefit wealthy people like 'tax advantage for the rich'.
- Look for concern that procedural rules prevent lawmakers from challenging a bill like 'no way of challenging a point of order'.
- Look for scrutiny of a housing bill’s tax provisions and their distributional effects like 'housing bill'.

text: Would not this amendment of the gentleman. increasing the amount by $45.000.000. be a financial saving to the National Government in the long run. in that it would encourage the States and local governments to do their part. because we have kept faith with them under the original authorization act?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for framing increased federal funding as a long-term financial saving when it encourages states and local governments to contribute.
- Look for support for federal-state cooperation like 'States and local governments'.
- Look for an appeal to honoring prior government commitments like 'kept faith'.

text: I do not care whether it is a rule of the House. it is just as wrong. I do not care if it has existed 100 years. it is still wrong. I am not blaming any Member. I am not criticizing any Member. I am denouncing it as wrong and as undemocratic.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for rejecting a long-standing institutional practice simply because it has existed for generations, like 'existed 100 years'.
- Look for framing procedural fairness and democratic principles as more important than House rules, like 'wrong and as undemocratic'.
- Look for distinguishing criticism of a practice from blame directed at individual lawmakers, like 'not blaming any Member', 'not criticizing any Member'.

text: I think that the report ought to be made. in view of the fact that the time has run over such a long period since the first Dies committee report was made. I think that Congress sought to be able to take action in the way of a positive enactment during this coming session.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for issuing a new report after a long delay, like 'time has run over'.
- Look for urging Congress to take concrete legislative action, like 'positive enactment'.
- Look for a focus on acting during the upcoming session, like 'this coming session'.

text: I have a parochial interest in consumers and also in poultry and dairy producers. who are of such great importance to the economy of my State. This question does not affect the economy of my State. but my recollection is that the corn farmers themselves voted against virtually the very program which the bill will institute. Am I incorrect?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for an emphasis on consumer interests alongside poultry and dairy producers, like 'consumers', 'poultry and dairy producers'.
- Look for concern about the economic importance of agricultural producers to the speaker’s state, like 'economy of my State'.
- Look for skepticism toward a proposed government program based on opposition from affected farmers, like 'corn farmers themselves voted against'.

text: But if the gentleman will inquire of the Secretary of Agriculture. he will find that going back to that program will cost immeasurably more. by the tens of millions of dollars. and that it would be unworkable in the view of the present Department of Agriculture. The gentlemans amendment should be rejected.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern about the high public cost of returning to an earlier program, citing 'tens of millions of dollars'.
- Look for reliance on expert agency judgment to assess whether a policy can work, citing 'present Department of Agriculture'.
- Look for framing an opponent’s proposal as impractical and urging its rejection, citing 'unworkable' and 'should be rejected'.

text: The Senator has in his memory that very good bills have been brought into the Senate. but the Senate will not pass them. I remember that the Senators bill was a just bill. and he was as confident of the necessity of it as I am of the necessity of this bill.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for passing legislation viewed as necessary and just.
- Look for frustration with the Senate for refusing to pass bills.
- Look for language emphasizing a lawmaker’s confidence in the necessity of a proposed bill.

text: How has it happened that the soldiers who he claims are improperly under the stigma of desertion have been so for the space of time that has elapsed since that aspersion was cast upon them. twenty years ago? Why has not the question been raised until this Mexican war pension bill has been brought before the Senate?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for challenging a long-standing accusation against soldiers branded as deserters.
- Look for questioning why the issue arose only when a pension bill was before the Senate.
- Look for concern about veterans’ reputations and eligibility for pensions.
- Look for skeptical scrutiny of claims made about soldiers in the context of the Mexican war pension bill.

text: Now. what I desire to call attention to is that the only way to reduce in a great degree the annual cost of pensions is to chEage the pension laws and declare that those who are now entitled to pensions under existing laws shall not hereafter be entitled to pensions.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for a call to reduce government spending by changing pension laws.
- Look for support for ending future pension eligibility under existing laws.
- Look for a focus on limiting public obligations to reduce annual costs.

text: Now. before the gentleman proceeds. I would like to ask him a question or two. He says that we ought to proceed upon this work with great care. If that is so. it means more investigation instead of actual work. Now. I want to call the gentlemans attention to the following plank in the platform of the Democratic party-
label: D
explanation:
- Look for invoking a party platform as authority, like 'platform of the Democratic party'
- Look for skepticism toward prolonged investigation when it delays action, like 'more investigation instead of actual work'
- Look for rhetoric favoring practical work over extended deliberation, like 'actual work'

text: Mr. Chairman. in the presentation of the debate the Republicans had onehalf the time. all of which they used against what we wanted and what the President wanted. The majority of the time on the Democratic side was against the bill. So 75 or 80 percent of the8 hours debate was against the bill.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for criticism that opponents used their debate time to oppose both the speaker’s agenda and the president’s.
- Look for emphasis that most debate time was spent against the bill.
- Look for framing that the bill had support from the speaker and president but faced extensive opposition.

text: Does not the gentleman know that the civil service law Is disregarded in every branch of this Government and particularly in the Post Office Department. and does not the gentleman know that there is no regard whatever paid to the civil service law in the appointment of postmasters or rural carriers throughout the country?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern about civil service protections being disregarded across government agencies.
- Look for opposition to patronage in federal appointments like 'appointment of postmasters'.
- Look for attention to fair hiring practices for public servants, including 'rural carriers'.

text: I thank the gentleman for yielding. I have noted each year what I consider to be fantastic increases in the costs of the Secret Service. I am pleased to hear the gentleman say. if I understood him correctly. that he hopes that Congress has now reached a plateau with respect to the increased costs of maintaining the Secret Service.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern about rising federal agency expenses, reflected in 'fantastic increases in the costs'.
- Look for support for limiting government spending growth through a 'plateau' in costs.
- Look for scrutiny of the costs of maintaining a federal protective service.

text: Mr. President. I sum up our position by saying the amendment of the Senator from Indiana turns an antirecession measure into an antidepression measure. We would have to get to a horrendous state of economic dislocation before his proposed unemployment rate would trigger the program into effect. Mr. President. I yield back the remainder of my time.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for activating economic relief before conditions reach a severe downturn.
- Look for concern that a high unemployment trigger would delay assistance until “horrendous state of economic dislocation”.
- Look for framing a measure as too limited to counter a deep economic crisis, as in “antirecession measure” versus “antidepression measure”.

text: Well. all right. Take it anyway the gentleman wants. Let me ask him this question. Has he ever heard of any more expensive way of kidding the American public than to try to grab $2 billion out of Uncle Sams Treasury right now to give back to the voters in order to buy their votes?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for framing direct payments from the Treasury to voters as an attempt to buy votes.
- Look for criticism of an expensive proposal to give money back to voters.
- Look for skepticism toward using public funds for immediate voter relief.

text: Mr. Chairman. I thank the gentleman for yielding. I think the amendment clearly says. "that nothing in the above provisos shall be construed to permit a labor organization to picket an employer." One employer. Not the site. The common situs can go on. It will not go on to just one employer who has this minority problem.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to labor organizations picketing an individual employer like 'picket an employer'.
- Look for a narrow interpretation of labor restrictions that distinguishes one employer from a shared worksite like 'One employer', 'Not the site'.
- Look for concern about allowing common-situs picketing to continue while restricting it against a specific employer like 'The common situs can go on'.

text: The resolution would authorize the Speaker to appoint a committee for the purpose of investigating subversive and unAmerican activities. in other words. activities that we as Americans do not approve of. something we do not stand for. I mean activities which would destroy our Constitution. or activities which advocate destroying our everyday life. Those are the things I am after.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for congressional investigations into alleged threats to constitutional order like 'destroy our Constitution'.
- Look for framing political scrutiny around whether activities match shared national values like 'do not stand for'.
- Look for broad language defining subversion through opposition to familiar ways of life like 'destroying our everyday life'.

text: Mr. Chairman and gentlemen of the committee. this bill carries the most liberal appropriations for the education. health. and industrial training and development of the Indians of any bill reported or passed since I .became a Member of Congress. If the Indians are to be brought to a state of selfsupport within a reasonable length of time. even
label: R
explanation:
- Look for emphasizing expanded public appropriations for education, health, and industrial training.
- Look for treating self-support as a goal for Indigenous communities.
- Look for framing the bill as unusually generous, like 'most liberal appropriations'.

text: I know the Senator from Wyoming does. too. but the major point of the Senator from Wyoming as I understand. is that if we are going to make that saving. then as a preventive of depression we ought to apply the $5.000.000.000 on the national debt rather than half of it on a taxreduction program.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for prioritizing debt reduction over a tax-reduction program like 'apply the $5.000.000.000 on the national debt'.
- Look for framing national debt repayment as a preventive measure against economic downturns like 'as a preventive of depression'.
- Look for skepticism toward using public savings for tax cuts like 'rather than half of it on a taxreduction program'.

text: Then it must follow. it seems to me. that the passage of the bill as it Is now would mean a claim upon the part of every railroad in the United States for every commodity that was ever included in any order of the President. Would not that be logical?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that legislation may impose broad liability on every railroad.
- Look for a focus on claims involving commodities covered by presidential orders.
- Look for rhetorical questioning to challenge the logical consequences of a bill.

text: I want to ask the gentleman from Texas if. after sober thought. just exactly the reverse would not be true? If this amendment were adopted and if a man did not waive any mortgage he. had. the Government would not make the loan. would it. because it could not be protected?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that a mortgage could prevent a borrower from receiving a government loan, as in 'Government would not make the loan'.
- Look for emphasis on whether the government can protect its loan when a borrower retains a mortgage, as in 'could not be protected'.
- Look for questioning whether the proposed amendment would create the opposite of its intended effect, as in 'just exactly the reverse'.

text: Yes. if he violates the law. that is so. But I am notfavorable to this practice of making the violation of some regulation of some department punishable as a crime. Mr. President. if I may be permitted to do so. I move to amend the amendment by striking out the words "or any regulations made under this act."
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to criminalizing violations of administrative regulations like 'punishable as a crime'.
- Look for skepticism toward broad agency rulemaking like 'regulations made under this act'.
- Look for a preference to distinguish statutory lawbreaking from violations of departmental rules.

text: Not at this point. I will yield later. The rights of depositors are important. They are of the greatest importance. The kind of right we want is the right for the depositor to know where his money goes. The depositor is the one who would be enlightened by this kind of information. I yield to the Senator.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for prioritizing depositors’ right to know how their money is used, like 'where his money goes'.
- Look for framing financial transparency as a way to inform and empower ordinary depositors, like 'would be enlightened'.
- Look for emphasizing consumer protections and depositor interests, like 'rights of depositors'.

text: I am sorry the Senator thinks that his record would be anything but complimentary to himself. I do not believe the Senator from Mississippi would disown his own record. and I believe the Senator will agree with me that his record on the tariff and on all other public matters reflects great credit on the Senator.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for a defense of a colleague’s legislative record as worthy of “great credit”.
- Look for an emphasis on a senator’s record “on the tariff” as a measure of public service.
- Look for respectful, collegial framing that avoids attacking the other senator personally.

text: The Senator propounded a question. and I am trying to answer him. Did we not cut it then to $6.800.003.000? Now we are talking about shortening the period from 15 months to 12 months. and of reducing the amount to $4.500.000.000. I say. tell the people the truth. the whole truth. and nothing but the truth.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for reducing government spending or the scale of a public program.
- Look for emphasis on shortening benefit or program timelines.
- Look for a focus on candor and accountability to the public like 'tell the people the truth'.
- Look for framing a proposal through specific budget figures and comparisons.

text: Mr. President. I ask permission to have printed in the RECORD a number of newspaper editorials and items in answer to remarks made in the Senate and elsewhere to the effect that we are not emerging from the depression. These clippings. furnishing evidence to the contrary. are selected at random from newspapers all over the United States.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for framing economic recovery as a matter of public evidence by citing newspaper editorials and items.
- Look for challenging claims of continued economic hardship with evidence of recovery like 'not emerging from the depression'.
- Look for drawing on newspapers from across the country to support a broad national perspective like 'all over the United States'.

text: Let me ask the gentleman from Arkansas. before he takes his seat. why it is necessary to employ seven men to make the allotments instead of a smaller number? It is very obvious that the original appropriation of $15.000 was sufficient. and nothing has been said today to disclose to the contrary.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for questioning the need for a large administrative staff when a smaller one may suffice.
- Look for arguing that the original appropriation was sufficient and seeking evidence for any claim that more funding is needed.

text: I see the point the Senator from Maryland makes. but. instead of exempting the tobacco. let us clarify the provisions of the bill. if we can agree on that. until we know that only the growers of Maryland tobacco No. 32 can vote on the question of the quota as it applies to that tobacco.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for narrowly tailored voting rules that limit quota decisions to growers directly affected by them.
- Look for a focus on protecting a specific regional agricultural constituency like 'growers of Maryland tobacco'.
- Look for an effort to clarify legislation rather than exempt a product outright like 'clarify the provisions of the bill'.

text: Because of the long experience of the gentleman from Nebraska with reclamation matters and public works projects. will he not agree with me that -the good folks back there in the first district of Kansas should be entitled to equally as good treatment as the Indians in Wyoming or in Montana?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for appeals to equal treatment for constituents across regions, like 'first district of Kansas'.
- Look for framing that compares constituent treatment with federal support for Indigenous communities, like 'the Indians in Wyoming'.
- Look for emphasis on local public works and reclamation expertise, like 'reclamation matters' and 'public works projects'.

text: It is absolute repudiation. My friend says it is extortion. I say it is just as much repudiation to require the people to pay more than the contract stipulates as it is to compel the creditor to take less. text: I thank the Senator. The purpose of the provision in the bill is to obtain new ideas. just as the purpose of any grant to investigate a problem is to study the problem to come up with new ideas to solve a serious problem which is growing critical in this country. is it not?

- Look for an emphasis on generating new ideas through publicly funded research.
- Look for framing a growing national problem as urgent and deserving of government study.

text: No. Mr. President. I believe they are the words of the Speaker of the other House. That is the most important provisionnot balancing the budget. not regulatory reform. not term limits. not school prayer. - Look for rejection of balancing the budget, regulatory reform, and term limits as the central priority.
- Look for a warning that all Americans should pay attention to who benefits from tax policy, like 'All the American people should be aware'.

text: Is it not better to resettle those people and keep them in their own homes where they have their own livestock and everything to work with? explanation:

- Look for support for modest public spending to help people stay in their communities like 'this small amount of money'.

text: I should like to have the Senator either confirm or reject the following statement: We were told that our balanceofpayments position during the past several years had markedly Improved. explanation:

- Look for criticism of asking other countries to make advance payments on their long-term debts.
- Look for concern about pressure on foreign creditors not to demand gold.
- Look for skepticism toward claims that the country’s financial position had “markedly Improved”.

text: Will the gentleman state. if lie knows. whether or not during the present administration. since the House and Senate and executive department have been Democratic. if any general pension legislation has become a law. or if it has not been entirely confined to special bills and no general legislation whatever?
label: R
explanation:

- Look for emphasis on whether general pension laws were enacted or whether relief was limited to special bills.
- Look for framing legislative inaction as the responsibility of the governing branches.

text: Even the professions of loyalty to the policy of a tariff for revenue. which ought to apply in the face of the awful competition with the Asiatic labor on these lines. will not. I imagine. cause gentlemen to hesitate a moment to fix things so that the cotton planter will never vote anything but the Democratic ticket.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for tariffs as a way to raise revenue.
- Look for concern about competition from lower-wage Asian labor.
- Look for appeals to the interests and voting behavior of cotton planters.
- Look for rhetorical framing that ties economic policy to partisan loyalty, like 'never vote anything but'.

text: I feel we ought to put some of this money we are spending in this period of time somewhere where there will be something to show for it. $175 million is not much waste. in my judgment. when you put it where it will save lives and also expedite commerce.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for public spending when it can save lives and improve commerce.
- Look for judging spending by whether it produces tangible benefits, as in 'something to show for it'.
- Look for treating $175 million as worthwhile when directed toward practical public benefits, rather than as waste.

text: The question is this. Mr. Chairman: If this bill becomes law. if it passes the House and is signed by the President. say. on August 1. 1970. would the Federal Government distribute funds under this bill to a State which had not through its legislative process agreed to contribute the 25 percent?

explanation:

- Look for scrutiny of the bill’s state-funding requirements like 'contribute the 25 percent'.
- Look for attention to the legislative process by which states decide whether to participate in a federal program.

text: That is the amendment that I hope will be disagreed to. because it makes a provision for overtime which will be a very embarrassing provision if it is made. It changes an existing condition. and it will lead to very great expenditure and an increase in the appropriations. in my judgment.

- Look for opposition to expanding overtime provisions based on concerns about increased government spending.
- Look for arguments that changing existing conditions would require greater appropriations and public expenditure.
- Look for concern about provisions being embarrassing or impractical as grounds for opposing an amendment.

text: This is a question purely for information. Does the gentleman recall when the social security bill was discussed on the floor of this House the point was ever raised that the cumulative fund was to be used for the purpose of liquidating the outstanding Government debt and reposing it in the reserve account?
label: R

- Look for attention to how Social Security reserves are managed, like 'reserve account'.
- Look for scrutiny of the government’s stated purpose for accumulating funds, like 'liquidating the outstanding Government debt'.

text: If that statement be trueand from the wording of this bill it seems to be truethen you have provided for a $7.500 salary for the representative which has been reduced to $5.000. by a recent amendment. and you have $4.000 plus as our share under the treaty. explanation:

- Look for comparing the representative’s reduced salary with the amount provided under the treaty.
- Look for asking for a transparent breakdown of public funds with 'What are the items'

text: One would think so. but the experience in Virginia has not been a happy one. Some would not work at all. Others would not work when they were certified as being trained. - Look for concern that training certifications may not translate into employment, like 'certified as being trained'.
- Look for attention to how unemployment benefits differ across states, especially when comparing a 'poverty stricken State'.

text: I would like to ask the gentleman In charge of the Vill a question. The entire purpose of the bill reported by the gentlemans committee is to designate the Board of United States General Appraisers as a court and give them that title? It does not change their duties. their personnel or the method of their appointment.

- Look for skepticism toward legislation that changes an agency’s status without changing its responsibilities.
- Look for scrutiny of whether a bill alters an institution’s duties, personnel, or appointment process.
- Look for questioning framed around the narrow purpose and practical effect of a bill.

text: No. I do not think the United Arab Republic is a friendly country. I do not think Mr. Nasser is a very friendly person. I am interested. however. in the national interest of the United States and in our interest in the Near East and our interest in the State of Israel.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for prioritizing the United States’ national interest in foreign policy.
- Look for concern with stability and strategic interests in the Near East.
- Look for explicit support for the security and interests of Israel.
- Look for a distinction between distrust of foreign leaders and attention to U.S. interests like 'national interest of the United States'.

text: Well. we did not have $12.000.000 surplus. We had a deficit. according to the PostOffice Department. of $13.000.000. and an actual deficit of $18.000.000. not thirteen. as reported to us by the Department. But. explanation:

- Look for emphasizing deficits over claims of surplus, like 'We had a deficit', 'an actual deficit'.
- Look for criticism that a public issue was neglected until a current official acted, like 'neglected for some years', 'took it up again'.

text: My personal opinion. Mr. President. If it is of any value to the Senator from North Carolina. is that the parcels post can not possibly be carried at a less cost than $30.000.000 to the Government more than is received ?rom it. I think the loss on parcel post is certainly $30.000.000. " 1925
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that a government service costs more to operate than it earns, like 'less cost than $30.000.000'.
- Look for emphasis on taxpayer-funded losses from public programs, like 'loss on parcel post'.
- Look for skepticism toward expanding government-run services when they impose substantial costs.

text: Mr. President. I inquire of the Senator if he can recall many appropriation bills where the Senate has reduced the amount of the appropriations proposed by the House. and where the conference report on an appropriation bill has shown a reduction of the amount below the amount carried by the bill as it passed the House?

explanation:
- Look for scrutiny of whether Senate appropriations are reduced below the amounts proposed or passed by the House.
- Look for attention to the Senate’s role in the budget process, especially conference reports on appropriation bills.
- Look for a questioning style that uses procedural precedent to challenge how public spending decisions are made.

text: I have a question on this Freedom Foundation group. I do not see any description of that group. Who appoints the members of the Commission. and so forth? I think we. as Members of Congress. ought to know who these people are. whether they are appointed for life or what the situation is.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward an organization whose membership and appointment process are unclear, like 'Who appoints the members'.
- Look for emphasizing congressional oversight and access to information about public commissions, like 'ought to know'.
- Look for concern about whether commission members serve indefinitely, like 'appointed for life'.

text: Oh. I quite agree with the gentleman on the general proposition. but if. as suggested by the gentleman from Mississippi [Mr. BowERS]. two men now having police powers have been detailed by the commissioners to enforce the law. they have the same responsibility that they would have if they were named under the appropriation act.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for enforcing the law through officials exercising police powers.
- Look for the view that officials detailed by commissioners bear the same responsibility as those named under an appropriation act.
- Look for a focus on the duties and accountability of public officials rather than broader social or economic policy.

text: But yet the Senator contends that. because we have not incorporated them into the Union. given them full benefit of American citizenship. or entered into negotiations to make them a State. even so we might dispose of our responsibility and cede to the Filipino people their liberty and the islands themselves?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for granting full American citizenship to people in territories.
- Look for opposition to ceding a people’s liberty without addressing the nation’s responsibility.
- Look for concern that territories should receive full benefits or be considered for statehood.
- Look for criticism of avoiding negotiations over a territory’s political status.

text: I think the proper word is "outrageous." We did try our best. as the Senator from New York is aware. I yield at this time to my distinguished colleague from Utah who was in the forefront and has always been in the forefront as far as the Eximbank is concerned.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for the Export-Import Bank, signaled by the reference to the “Eximbank”.
- Look for praise of a colleague’s leadership on a federal export-credit institution, as in “forefront”.
- Look for an appeal to bipartisan collegiality through respectful references to a colleague from another state, such as “distinguished colleague”.
- Look for forceful criticism framed as “outrageous.”

text: I discover a degree of weariness all over that side of the Chamber. I do not wonder [addressing the Republican side] that you are weary. I do not wonder that you rise in righteous protest against anything that calls attention to the unccncealable.iuquities of this the most iniquitous measure that was ever considered by a paaliamentary body.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for condemning the measure as deeply unjust, using moral language like 'righteous protest', 'most iniquitous measure'.
- Look for framing criticism as exposing wrongdoing that opponents would rather keep hidden, like 'calls attention to the unccncealable.iuquities'.
- Look for portraying opponents’ protests as a defensive reaction to scrutiny, like 'you are weary'.

text: The gentleman could not answer it except to say that it would not be germane to his amendment. But the proposal of the gentleman from Georgia is just another group protection. If you do it to my neighbor. it will be all right. but If you do it to me. it will not be so good.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward proposals framed as group-specific protections.
- Look for an appeal to equal treatment between neighbors and oneself like 'my neighbor', 'to me'.

text: But if there is a conflict between two people. he may not have interjected his lifestyle into the public. but he may be in trouble with another individual. Is the gentleman saying therefore that no one accused in a civil court who is a claimed homosexual can get defense on a cause involving a homosexual claim?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for defending access to legal representation for people accused in civil court.
- Look for concern about whether a person's private identity affects their ability to get a defense like 'claimed homosexual'.
- Look for framing the issue as a conflict between two individuals rather than public conduct like 'conflict between two people'.

text: So the Senator from South Carolina believes. does he. that such a requirement by the State of Massachusettsnamely. that all persons who wished to vote would first have to have passed an examination given by Harvard Universityor even a requirement that all voters would first have to have graduated from Harvard Universitywould be permissible?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for opposition to educational tests as a prerequisite for voting.
- Look for concern that states might restrict voting through requirements like 'passed an examination'.
- Look for criticism of tying voter eligibility to elite credentials like 'graduated from Harvard University'.

text: Mr. Speaker. I see a provision in this bill reserving the right to Congress to alter or amend this charter at any time. I wish to know whether the committee understand that this reserves to Congress the right to regulate the fares on this road whenever it shall so choose?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for congressional authority to regulate private transportation fares.
- Look for scrutiny of charter provisions that reserve Congress’s power to “alter or amend” them.

text: Is it the intent of this amendment that the producers would be able to have enough incentive and enough profit at the regulated interstate price? That is where the price would be. All gas would be regulated at the interstate price. This provides they plow back any profits above that?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for regulating natural gas prices across interstate markets like 'regulated interstate price'.
- Look for concern about ensuring producers still have enough incentive and profit under price regulation.
- Look for allowing regulated producers to retain profits only if they reinvest amounts above the regulated level like 'plow back any profits'.

text: As I understand it. this amendment meets the argument that we have simply handed over our discretion as a Congress. in the committee amendment. to the head of OMB. In other words. we said any cut between zero and 5 percent. Here the Senator from Oklahoma is saying that the cut shall be 2 percent. is that correct?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern about Congress handing over its budget discretion to the executive branch, as in 'handed over our discretion'.
- Look for support for a fixed spending cut rather than leaving the cut to executive officials, as in 'the cut shall be 2 percent'.
- Look for scrutiny of broad administrative authority, especially when an agency head can choose the size of a budget cut.

text: Mr. Speaker. not only do I want to thank all of you and all of the Senate for this day. making it possible for women to be considered as human beings under the Constitution. but also I wear these flowers today to celebrate the fact that Hawaii is the first State to ratify the equal rights amendment.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for constitutional equality for women, like 'women to be considered as human beings'.
- Look for celebration of state ratification of an equal-rights amendment, like 'Hawaii is the first State to ratify'.

text: Then let me say that today I received from a lawyer a letter in which he asks whether it is the normal procedure for the chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee to announce his support of the treaty before he heard one word from anyone about itwhile he was In Moscow.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for scrutiny of a committee chairman’s public support for a treaty before hearing any views.
- Look for concern about officials announcing a position on foreign policy while abroad.
- Look for emphasis on deliberation and hearing arguments before endorsing an agreement.
- Look for rhetorical questioning of whether a procedure is normal like 'normal procedure'.

text: No: not the Independence. There may have been a few trips the Independence has made that were not on official business. but. almost without exception. when I have read of the trips the President has made in the Independence. they have been official business trips. These trips save time. money. and great inconvenience to the public.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for defending the president’s use of official travel as a way to save public money and avoid inconvenience.
- Look for emphasizing efficiency in government travel, like 'save time', 'money'.
- Look for distinguishing official business from nonofficial trips to justify use of public resources.

text: Mr. President. I want the Senator to go ahead and see how ridiculous he is making himself by these dilatory motions and dilatory quorums. and perhans the patience of the Senate eventually will wear itself out. even those who do not believe it is dilatory do not wear themselves out.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for criticism of procedural delays, such as 'dilatory motions', 'dilatory quorums'.
- Look for frustration with tactics that waste the Senate’s time and test its patience.

text: But let us understand this provision. The Senator sees it very clearly. I do not. An alien comes here in advance of his family. Are you going to assess only $4 on him because he has a "wife and children in Europe who are coming here? Is that the idea?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward charging an immigrant a lower fee based on family members expected to join them, like 'wife and children in Europe'.
- Look for concern about how immigration fees are assessed for people arriving in advance of their families, like 'assess only $4'.
- Look for rhetorical questioning that challenges a provision’s fairness or logic, like 'Is that the idea?'

text: Mr.. Speaker.. reserving tle right to. object. this. of course. is the- annual measure that is passed: each year. and. certainly there is no urgency about that and no. particular reason why it should be given preference over this great einergency war measure.. for- which we adopted a special rule the other day. and I will object.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to prioritizing a routine annual measure over an emergency war measure.
- Look for framing a war measure as urgent, like 'great einergency war measure'.
- Look for emphasizing that a recurring annual measure is not urgent, like 'no urgency about that'.
- Look for objecting to giving a routine measure preference over a special-rule measure, like 'I will object'.

explanation:
- Look for using public authorities to take over rail infrastructure when private railroads go bankrupt.
- Look for supporting revenue bonds to help recapitalize bankrupt railroads.
- Look for a federal legislative role in preserving regional transportation infrastructure.

text: Will the Senator from Virginia allow me to remind the Senator from New York that the Government promised to pay one dollar in the note which I hold in my hand. at no time or in anything. bat simply "one dollar." and yet this note is within two per cent. of gold.

explanation:
- Look for an emphasis on the government honoring its promise to repay a debt at face value, like 'Government promised to pay'.
- Look for a defense of the note’s value by comparing it favorably with gold, like 'within two per cent. of gold'.
- Look for a focus on the precise wording of a financial obligation rather than broader claims about repayment, like 'simply "one dollar."'.

text: Under the new rules which have been referred to by the gentleman from Pennsylvania can a man now go and voluntarily enlist under the new ruling and designate the service where he would like to serve and have any degree of certainty of serving in the service with this equalizing rule in effect?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern about whether an enlistment rule preserves individual choice over military service.
- Look for attention to certainty about which service a volunteer will join.
- Look for scrutiny of an “equalizing rule” and its effect on voluntary enlistment.

text: Does not the gentleman think it would be better. if we are to adopt a system of laws at variance with the entire minerallaw system of the United States. to bring the measure up as an original proposition. and discuss it as such. rather than tack it onto an appropriation bill?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for procedural criticism of attaching major policy changes to an appropriation bill.
- Look for concern that the measure conflicts with the “entire minerallaw system”.
- Look for preference to introduce the measure as an “original proposition”.
- Look for emphasis on debating policy “as such” rather than folding it into unrelated legislation.

text: And I say to the gentleman that we should not be considering it at all. We should have gone home. The country wants this Congress to adjourn. The country does not want it to sit here indulging in the expenditure of any more of the taxpayers money. I insist upon my motion.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for opposition to continued congressional spending, framed as “expenditure of any more”.
- Look for concern for taxpayers and public spending, like 'taxpayers money'.
- Look for a call to end the session because “The country wants this Congress to adjourn.”

text: The Senate provision left this bridge open to all street railway companies that wanted to cross. and took the control entirely away from Congress. label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that legislation could remove congressional oversight by taking “the control entirely away from Congress”.
- Look for opposition to a blanket entitlement for all companies, framed as avoiding “a general omnibus right”.
- Look for support for protecting an established operator’s existing access while limiting new access to “the right of this road”.

text: I would like to think that we both have a chance at it when the windfall profits tax comes up. That is all I am thinking. Will the Senator agree that this would be an amendment in the first degree for the purpose of amendment? Original text is even better.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to a windfall profits tax, signaled by “windfall profits tax”.
- Look for interest in amending legislation and shaping its original text.
- Look for procedural language focused on the amendment’s status and priority, such as “first degree”.

text: Mr. Speaker. I would like to ask the gentlelen in charge of this resolution why it is that it has beet brought in at this late hour. when there are practically no Members of the house here. when they had all day to bring this in. at a time when we had a large attendance here?

explanation:
- Look for criticism of introducing a resolution when few lawmakers are present.
- Look for emphasis on the missed opportunity to bring the measure forward earlier, when attendance was higher.
- Look for concern about legislative timing and the ability of members to participate.

text: May I ask the Senator if there is not some repQrt from the Secretary of the Treasury which shows specifically the diminution of these sources of revenue and the causes therefor. and. as it is supposed. of the increaqe of the expenses under another head. so as to require an increase of the standing appropriation ?

explanation:
- Look for scrutiny of Treasury reports documenting changes in revenue sources and their causes.
- Look for concern that rising expenses under another heading could require a larger standing appropriation.
- Look for a request for specific fiscal evidence before accepting an increase in government funding.

text: Mr. Speaker. I have filed with the Clerk of the House a petition to bring out of the Rules Committee the bill for the relief of the widows. orphans. and dependent parents. of deceased veterans of the World War. and at this point I ask unanimous consent to insert the bill in the RECORD.

- Look for support for financial relief for families of deceased veterans.
- Look for a constituent focus on widows, orphans, and dependent parents.
- Look for using a petition to move veterans’ relief legislation out of committee.

text: Has anything authoritative come from our representatives at the peace conference indicative of a purpose upon their part so to pledge the future of the United States--that is. commit it to a policy that would compel this Nation to guarantee tile territorial integrity of nations that may be set up as the result of the breaking up of central Europe?

explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward binding international commitments that would guarantee other nations’ territorial integrity.
- Look for concern that a peace conference could commit the United States to a future foreign policy.
- Look for emphasis on protecting national sovereignty from obligations arising from the breakup of Central Europe.

text: Mr. Speaker. is not the legitimate qonclusion of this report of this conference committee that it is a frank statement of failure on their part to adjust differences. with the result that instead of trying to adjust differences they strike out the whole provision altogether? label: R
explanation:
- Look for criticism of a conference committee for failing to reconcile differences.
- Look for framing the committee’s action as abandoning the entire provision rather than resolving disagreements, like 'strike out the whole provision'.
- Look for emphasis on the committee’s admitted inability to reach agreement, like 'unable to adjust differences'.

text: Mr. Chairman. I think we ought to have this amendment in. because it says to authorize for sale at not less than the appraised value. It does not say for what. It might be sale for stock in the Tube Co. It might be sold for some other consideration. The words "for cash." I think. should be inserted.

explanation:
- Look for requiring cash payment rather than vague or noncash consideration like 'for cash'.
- Look for protecting public assets by insisting sales meet appraised value like 'not less than the appraised value'.
- Look for concern about ambiguity in the terms of a transaction like 'It does not say for what'.

text: Rust bucket is a misrepresentation. Do not tell us that. We have had experts all over these ships. The engineering system works beautifully. They are not rust buckets. explanation:
- Look for defending military equipment against criticism by citing expert inspections.
- Look for emphasizing the engineering reliability of naval vessels.
- Look for framing battleships’ long service life as evidence of their value.

text: Before I am led off into this. let me say that I have not the figures on this exportable wheat from the Pacific coast. and I do not know just what they charge. - Look for attention to whether tariffs provide substantial protection to domestic producers.
- Look for a hypothetical argument that explicitly states its assumptions.

text: And because that expenditure. controlled by the Legislature of Alaska. is forbidden by Federal statute. this bill proposes to repeal that provision. so far as these particular" expenditures go. explanation:
- Look for support for state legislative control over how funds are spent.
- Look for opposition to federal restrictions on state spending.
- Look for framing federal repeal as letting local lawmakers act freely, like 'get out of the way'.

text: Mr. Speaker. before the gentleman takes his seat will he allow me to suggest there is one other bad feature about this bill. and that is it proposes to take $300.000 out of a depleted Treasury in order to make entertainment for people somewhere. which the people of the United States will not even have an opportunity to attend themselves.

- Look for concern that federal spending benefits people “somewhere” rather than serving the public broadly.
- Look for framing government expenditure as wasteful when it funds entertainment instead of addressing public needs.

explanation:
- Look for framing voters’ approval of a tax-limiting measure as a revolt against government taxation.
- Look for portraying taxpayers as overburdened and demanding relief, like 'enough is enough', 'tax nightmare'.
- Look for urging Congress to heed voter anger over taxes and respond to taxpayers’ concerns.

text: Let me interrupt the gentleman for a moment. as I would like an explanation of what he means when he speaks of giving this to "the treatymaking power." I understand this fund is to be taken into a sort of secretservice arrangement. The Senate has nothing to do with it.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that a fund is being placed under a “secretservice arrangement.”
- Look for skepticism toward concentrating authority in the treaty-making power.
- Look for emphasis on the Senate’s lack of oversight, as in “The Senate has nothing to do with it.”

text: Yes. it would come nearer reducing the cost of living than the tariff bill did. The Senator from Mississippi seems to be very much opposed to the Government undertaking to do anything that would benefit tile people if it comes il collflict with any of his preconceived theories of things.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for government action that reduces the cost of living.
- Look for criticism of rigid economic theories when they conflict with policies benefiting the public.
- Look for framing policy by whether it directly benefits ordinary people.

text: That was enough for the rich planters of Cuba. who must have the best class of wheat in their flour. They were able to buy it. but so far as the mass of the people in Cuba were concerned. they could not buy our flour until the duty was reduced to 90 cents a barrel.

explanation:
- Look for concern about reducing import duties to make goods more affordable for ordinary consumers, as in 'duty was reduced'.
- Look for a contrast between wealthy buyers and the broader population, as in 'rich planters' and 'mass of the people'.
- Look for attention to expanding access to domestic products in foreign markets by lowering trade barriers, as in 'buy our flour'.

text: Well. that is not exactly what the bill provides. In reply to the Senator. it does not provide for supervision of hiring.
