label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for preventing discrimination in state and local government employment.
- Look for a preference for federal-state cooperation to enforce equal treatment, like 'work together with the States'.
- Look for attention to hiring practices and employment protections, like 'supervision of hiring', 'not discrimination'.

text: Where does the gentleman get the idea that. the political support of the South was a matter of barter and sale? Have we not demonstrated throughout our history our fidelity to principle by standing out in the cold for years? The gentleman has made the suggestion that we can be bought and sold like cattle.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for rejecting the idea that political support is a matter of transactional “barter and sale”.
- Look for emphasizing a history of “fidelity to principle” over political expediency.
- Look for forceful rhetoric against treating constituents or political allies as “bought and sold like cattle”.

text: Oh. no. that would be responsible principle. I want those words to be impressed upon the Secretary. The proposals which the administration will make next year will be timed. incidentally. before the elections. This will be a fulfillment of the highest responsibility of public office. with plenty of piety and pontifical pronouncement. make no mistake about it.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that policy proposals may be timed to influence elections, like 'before the elections'.
- Look for framing public office as a matter of responsibility and principle, like 'highest responsibility'.
- Look for skepticism toward administration announcements wrapped in moralizing rhetoric, like 'plenty of piety', 'pontifical pronouncement'.

text: I wish to strongly endorse the amendment offered by the gentleman from Wisconsin . Those who believe that a public works bill should be passed can insure enactment by adopting this amendment. The item veto is a recommendation of the Hoover Commission. It would permit the President to eliminate those porkbarrel projects which make this a bad bill.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for giving the president an item veto to remove individual spending projects.
- Look for criticism of public works spending as porkbarrel projects.
- Look for using the Hoover Commission’s recommendation to support limits on government spending.
- Look for framing amendment adoption as a way to improve a flawed spending bill.

text: Mr. Speaker. who does the gentleman mean by the word "they" ? Who is taking on the responsibility for spending this $95.000? Is it a commisslon to be appointed. or a body or group of men. to take on this responsibility. or who will have the authority to expend this money and put on this celebration?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for scrutiny of government spending and demands for accountability over who controls public funds, like 'responsibility for spending'.
- Look for concern about public money being spent on a celebration, like 'expend this money' and 'this celebration'.
- Look for insistence on identifying who has authority over expenditures, like 'who will have the authority'.

text: I am very glad that the gentleman makes this statement. because. as a fact. the McKinley tariff act puts on the free list nearly all the materials required in the construction of vessels for the foreign trade. and thereby does all that it is possible to do by tariff legislation to aid in the construction of these vessels.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for free-list tariff exemptions on materials used to build vessels for foreign trade like 'puts on the free list'.
- Look for using tariff legislation to promote domestic shipbuilding and maritime trade like 'aid in the construction'.

text: It was done In the city of New York. and it brought the greatest run upon the bank that did it that was ever known in the financial history of the country. I will undertake to say that in a large majority of the cases where savings banks have resorted to that rule they have brought a run on themselves.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that a bank’s own policies can trigger a damaging run on deposits.
- Look for emphasis on the risks of savings banks adopting rules that undermine depositor confidence.
- Look for framing a financial practice as a threat to the stability of the banking system.
- Look for citing a dramatic historical bank run to argue against the policy that caused it.

text: Second. that Senator Morgan vainly sought to have the Senate strike Article VI from the Platt amendment because. undisputed by any of his colleagues. he voiced the conviction that the inclusion of Article VI in the Platt amendment would forever make impossible the acquisition of the Isle of Pines as American territory.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for acquiring additional territory to expand national influence.
- Look for concern that a treaty provision could prevent territorial acquisition like 'forever make impossible'.
- Look for treating the Isle of Pines becoming American territory as a desirable goal like 'as American territory'.

text: Is it not true that while cotton was selling for 61/2 cents in America on the old gold basis. yet the Frenchman was buying cotton at 61/2 cents in gold. and after devaluation he could continue to pay 61/2 cents in gold. but the American farmer was getting 10 cents? Is that not true?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern about how currency devaluation affects domestic farmers’ prices and competitiveness.
- Look for comparisons between American farmers and foreign buyers, like 'the American farmer' and 'the Frenchman'.
- Look for attention to cotton prices and the gold basis, like '61/2 cents' and 'old gold basis'.

text: It is already in the bill. If the gentleman would yield further. those threshold requirements are already in the legislation. It is not a matter of placing them in my amendment. The thresholds that already exist are now simply going to cover approximately 150 additional substances which may have chronic longterm impact in the same way.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for expanding existing regulatory thresholds to cover additional substances with chronic long-term impacts.
- Look for a preference for building on safeguards already in legislation rather than duplicating them in an amendment.
- Look for emphasis on protecting people from the potential long-term effects of a wider range of substances.

text: Mr. Speaker. I desire to bring to the attention of the gentleman who has charge of that bill the language of the bill-" improper " and "unnecessary." That is very broad. and then the closing paragraph of the bill leaves this matter to the judgment of the Commissioner without any appeal.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that vague statutory language could grant officials overly broad discretion like 'improper', 'unnecessary'.
- Look for concern about giving a government commissioner unchecked authority without a path to challenge the decision like 'without any appeal'.
- Look for scrutiny of broad bill language and the safeguards available to people affected by administrative decisions.

text: I will be glad to. The purpose of this bill is to save time and money and also promote efficiency in the operation of the Patent Office. The Patent Office Is Issuing approximately 40.000 patents a year. There are 15 linotype. machines at the Government Printing Office engaged in doing
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for government-agency efficiency through saving time and money and streamlining operations.
- Look for attention to public institutions like the Patent Office and Government Printing Office.
- Look for a practical, administrative framing focused on patent processing and printing capacity.
- Look for emphasis on measurable government output like '40.000 patents a year'.

text: I wish to ask the Senator from Utah a question. Why should we repeal a law that has been shown to be so efficient as to absolutely prevent the frauds of which the Senator speaks? Why does he now want to try some other law and abandon the law that has proven sufficient?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for retaining an existing law because it is portrayed as effective at preventing fraud, like 'proven sufficient'.
- Look for skepticism toward replacing a law that is described as efficient and successful, like 'abandon the law'.
- Look for framing policy changes as unnecessary when the current law is said to prevent the problem, like 'prevent the frauds'.

text: As I say. the people outside the District of Columbia. the people back home own most of what is in the District of Columbia. and they have paid for most of it. and so I want the people back home to have something to say about how the District of Columbia is run.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for prioritizing residents outside the capital in decisions about how the district is governed, like 'people back home'.
- Look for framing the district as property funded and owned by people beyond its borders, like 'paid for most of it'.
- Look for advocating greater influence for people outside the district over its local governance, like 'something to say'.

text: That is what I have reference to. and I consider it vicious. A newspaper man. in the performance of his ordinary work of news gathering. if these words are permitted to remain in the bill. can be arrested and receive all of the penalties prescribed in the bill for those who distribute the prizefight films.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that broad criminal penalties could sweep in ordinary journalistic activity.
- Look for criticism of treating routine news gathering like distributing prohibited material.
- Look for defense of press freedom against vague or overly broad legislation.
- Look for framing the bill’s treatment of journalists as unjust or excessive like 'vicious'.

text: I. am very glad the Senator has called attention to those treaties in which the Monroe doctrine has been reserved. Those are arbitration treaties. Those are treaties under which we agree to submit to arbitration certain questions. We do not agree in the pending treaty to submit anything to arbitration.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for arbitration treaties that submit certain international disputes to arbitration.
- Look for a distinction between agreements to arbitrate specified questions and the pending treaty, which he says submits nothing to arbitration.
- Look for a foreign-policy argument framed around preserving the Monroe Doctrine in treaties.

text: As I understand. after those joint hearings the bill that was recommended to the House by the House committee was materially different from this bill in many respects. Evidently. then. the House committee does not feel it essential that the House accept the judgment of the Senate in this matter.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward accepting the Senate’s judgment without independent House review.
- Look for emphasis on the House committee’s role in evaluating legislation.
- Look for framing the bill’s differences from the committee recommendation as a reason for caution.

text: I beg the gentlemans pardon for interrupting. but I think the Republicans have not changed their position. We object to the legislation because it does not provide for hearings of those affected by the agreement. Neither does it provide for ratification by the Senate. Otherwise we are in accord with the legislation proposed today.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that legislation omits hearings for people affected by an agreement, like 'hearings of those affected'.
- Look for insistence that the Senate must ratify an agreement, like 'ratification by the Senate'.
- Look for framing opposition around procedural safeguards while expressing agreement with the broader proposal, like 'Otherwise we are in accord'.

text: It is quite obvious. I think. there is no chance to pass this inheritance tax on down to anyone or anywhere. It is the final contribution of the wealth that America makes possible to the common good of the America. that remains after the owner of the wealth is gone.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for framing inheritance taxation as a final contribution to the common good.
- Look for support for taxing wealth passed on after its owner dies.
- Look for emphasis on wealth as something made possible by America and owed partly to the public good.

text: The point of all this is that there are Members of the Senate who have not had the high privilege of hearing this debate. who have dashed in here and made speeches and defended what is being done on the ground that the Senate is faced with two certificates. but that is not the situation. is It?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for challenging the claim that the Senate is faced with only two certificates.
- Look for questioning the basis for defending actions taken on the ground.
- Look for emphasizing that some senators missed the debate before speaking.

text: Very well. I shall leave the amendment as it is. and I shall resist any amendment to increase the salaries of the President. the Vice President. and Members of Congress. as well as any special provisions other than those which are extended to businessmen. I shall insist on a vote on the amendment.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to raising salaries for elected officials.
- Look for resistance to special benefits for public officials beyond those available to businesspeople.
- Look for a preference to leave an amendment unchanged and insist on a recorded vote.

text: Does not the original joint resolution raise as much question. and recognize as having as much force the contention that Mr. Kennedy is not eligible. as the proposed amended form of resolution? Both of them are predicated upon a doubt as to eligibility. which the Senate is desirous of removing.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern about a candidate’s constitutional eligibility.
- Look for a preference for resolving doubt about eligibility through a Senate resolution.
- Look for scrutiny of both the original and amended forms of a resolution.

text: It would apply in that instance. It would apply to CARE. It would apply to the Red Cross. which certainly is not a religious organization. It would apply to charitable activities of the Salvation Army. which may be deemed a religious organization but also does charitable work. It would certainly apply to the Salvation Army.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for extending policy protections to charitable activities, regardless of an organization’s religious identity.
- Look for concern that broadly written rules could affect organizations such as 'the Red Cross'.
- Look for attention to the practical consequences of policy for both secular and faith-based service providers.
- Look for framing that distinguishes religious identity from charitable work, as in 'also does charitable work'.

text: If it is simply for the benefit of a sawmill. and there is nothing except 10 tons outside of the timber and logs. I should say that the condition of Mattawan Creek Is precisely on the same level. As to the policy of making an improvement for the purpose of benefiting a particular institution. I should disagree to that.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for opposition to public improvements designed to benefit a particular institution, like 'benefiting a particular institution'.
- Look for skepticism toward infrastructure spending justified by a narrow private benefit, like 'benefit of a sawmill'.
- Look for weighing the scale of a proposed improvement against limited commercial activity, like '10 tons'.

text: I heard the remark of the Senator from Virginia that the.currency association would examine them. How do you know that a currency association to be composed of a .majority of State banks and trust companies. and possibly dominated by that majority of State banks and trust companies. would examine with the degree of particularity which is necessary?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for skepticism about whether a currency association dominated by state banks and trust companies would provide sufficiently thorough oversight.
- Look for concern about the effectiveness of private financial institutions examining one another.

text: I understood the Senator to say that a large sum of money. representing tax exempts held by corporations. is made up chiefly of these certificates of indebtedness and these shorttime notes. and that the corporations did not pay any tax on the income derived from those securities. that they were totally exempt.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for criticism of corporations receiving tax-free income from securities.
- Look for attention to tax-exempt certificates of indebtedness and short-term notes like 'these shorttime notes'.
- Look for questioning whether corporate income from investments should be exempt from taxation.

text: I will say to the gentleman I do not think there will be any danger of the South American countries coming to us as suppliants. and I do not think it would be wise for us to put in" European Governments." I have no idea that the emergency or the occasion will occur that the gentleman anticipates.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward claims that South American countries will seek U.S. assistance, like 'coming to us as suppliants'.
- Look for opposition to inserting a reference to European governments into the measure, like 'put in" European Governments."'.
- Look for caution about legislating for a speculative crisis, like 'the occasion will occur'.

text: I say now that I am prepared to stand by my statement that if the Government undertakes to guarantee all the unusual risks on private investments of $20.000.000.000 a year in plants and machinery..which Mr. Wallace seems to contemplate. the Government will lose $4.000.000.000 a year. My estimate is very conservative. I think. under the conditions I have stated.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward government guarantees for private investment and concern about taxpayer losses.
- Look for emphasis on the financial risks of government intervention in private industry, like 'Government will lose'.
- Look for a cautious, cost-focused argument that frames the estimate as conservative, like 'very conservative'.

text: No matter. if a man served 90 days. and he dies now from any cause. whether from violence or anything else. say natural causes or disease. the mere fact that she is a widow of a soldier who served 90 days in the war and has not $250 entitles her to a pension?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for widows’ pensions based on a veteran’s service and the widow’s limited means, rather than the cause of death.
- Look for a focus on protecting financially vulnerable survivors like 'she is a widow'.
- Look for eligibility framed around military service, including 'served 90 days' and 'in the war'.
- Look for concern with a widow’s poverty, highlighted by 'has not $250'.

text: It is very small in amount. we ought to rectify it. and the judges ought to have their expenses when away from home. I would like the same law to apply to all judges as far as expenses are concerned. I do not believe that their salaries ought to be increased.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for equal treatment of judges on expense reimbursement.
- Look for a distinction between reimbursing judges’ expenses and increasing their salaries.
- Look for concern about limiting public compensation, like 'salaries ought to be increased'.

text: My colleague sat In on all the hearings. He was very diligent in his attendance. I listened to many of them. I will say that there is not a single bit of testimony in opposition. As a matter of fact. all the witnesses were quite concerned over the fact that these projects might not go forward.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for a claim that hearing witnesses unanimously supported moving projects forward, as in 'not a single bit of testimony in opposition'.
- Look for concern that projects could stall, as in 'might not go forward'.
- Look for emphasis on diligent participation in hearings, as in 'very diligent in his attendance'.

text: The cost of this Agency for 1 year is about the same as what it takes to produce one jetplane. We are supplying jetplanes to other countries to assist in our own defense. Yet. here. we cannot spend $10 million. the cost of one jetplane. to help to bring peace to the world.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for framing foreign assistance as a modest cost compared with military spending, like 'one jetplane'.
- Look for support for spending public funds to promote peace abroad, like 'bring peace to the world'.
- Look for presenting international aid as serving both humanitarian goals and national security, like 'assist in our own defense'.

text: In my previous colloquy with the gentleman from Georgia. I pointed out that there was no category of health and safety data. including that which might fall under the new and innovative technology definition. which was suppressed. that it was all available. It was available to the very people who said it was being suppressed from them.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for emphasizing public access to health and safety data and rejecting claims that it is being withheld.
- Look for noting that data on “new and innovative technology” was “all available”.

text: I said a few moments ago that in order that the worker shall be subject to regulation in his minimum wage under this bill. it must be shown that he is so far engaged in interstate commerce as to be a producer of a part of the working machinery of that system.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for regulating minimum wages only when a worker is sufficiently involved in interstate commerce.
- Look for emphasis on workers being 'subject to regulation' under the bill.
- Look for a narrow interpretation of federal authority based on whether a worker is 'a producer' within the interstate system.

text: Mr. Chairman. the warrevenue measure which was framed to meet the extraordinary expenditures caused by the war with Spain is now under consideration after that war is ended. For that war another war has been substituted. involving an extraordinary train of expenditures. in continuation of those made during the Spanish war.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for opposition to continuing extraordinary war spending after the original conflict has ended.
- Look for concern that one war has been replaced by another, prolonging public expenditures.
- Look for scrutiny of whether a revenue measure designed for wartime remains justified once the war is over.

text: Mr. President. my amendment would delete $13 million from the $96 million increase requested for the economic development revolving fund. This $13 million is the amount that EDA would use to support a $63.5 million loan guarantee for a new steel rail mill for the WheelingPittsburgh Steel Corp. Mr. President. may we have order?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for reducing federal spending by cutting part of an economic development fund increase.
- Look for skepticism toward federal support for a private steel mill through a loan guarantee like 'loan guarantee'.
- Look for concern about directing public funds to a specific corporation like 'WheelingPittsburgh Steel Corp'.

text: I say. sir. that as you put this mass of ignorance upon us. as you emancipated the colored people and made their children voters of the country. there is an obligation upon you. a high moral obligation. too. to help to contributeto the education of those people. and to fit them for the conduct of the Government.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for public education as a duty owed to newly enfranchised citizens.
- Look for concern that voters should be prepared to participate in government.
- Look for moral language framing education as a collective obligation.
- Look for attention to the education and civic inclusion of formerly enslaved people, like 'emancipated the colored people'.

text: I only know that when we got into it. and when the bloodletting began. we spentaccording to the figures of the Defense Establishment-$19 billion. in Korea. We did not seem to hesitate then about spending $125 per capita125 for every man. woman. and child in the United Statesto fight a war.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for framing military spending as justified despite its high per-person cost, like 'spending $125 per capita'.
- Look for using the scale of war spending to argue that the country did not hesitate to fund the conflict, like 'We did not seem to hesitate'.
- Look for highlighting the human cost of conflict alongside its financial cost, like 'the bloodletting began'.

text: First thanking the gentleman very much for the gracious reference made to my speech. which was far more than it deserved. let me ask this question: Is it nclt a fact that the lawyer and graduate of West Point who drew the conscription law against which the gentleman voted is to be the economic dictator under this bill?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for criticism of a bill that would place economic authority in the hands of a single appointed official.
- Look for concern that a lawyer and West Point graduate would become an “economic dictator”.
- Look for framing the conscription law as an objectionable precedent for evaluating the bill.

text: Mr. Speaker. If the gentleman will listen to the facts. I was Just coming to it. As of January 1 this year. the Defense Department had filled 11.080 of the 11.648 authorized physician slots for fiscal year 1977. So. there is no shortage. There are some 500 slots that are not filled out of almost 12.000.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for using staffing figures to argue that a claimed physician shortage is not supported by the facts.
- Look for distinguishing unfilled positions from a shortage, noting that only about 500 of nearly 12,000 slots were vacant.
- Look for framing the issue around Defense Department staffing and authorized physician positions.

text: Second. there are many who believe a narrower unfair competition model is preferable to the model set forth in the Coble bill. One such proposal has been proposed by certain commercial database users. with the support of the scientific. education. and library communities. I ask unanimous consent that this proposal also be printed in the RECORD.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for skepticism toward an expansive unfair-competition model and support for a narrower alternative.
- Look for favorable attention to commercial database users’ proposal.
- Look for emphasis on scientific, educational, and library communities as stakeholders.

text: The amount allowed for rivers and harbors and flood control is above the amount that the administration requested by a little over $30 million. The amount allowed for the Atomic Energy Commission. however. is below the amount requested by the Eisenhower administration. So that the overall picture probably is this-
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for higher-than-requested funding for rivers, harbors, and flood control.
- Look for a willingness to approve spending above the administration’s request for local infrastructure needs.
- Look for restraint in funding federal agencies, like 'below the amount requested'.
- Look for framing the spending comparison around the administration’s budget requests.

text: This bill proposes virtually to reenact the act of 1866. but with reference to public lands in the State of Alabama alone. That lawas originally passed applied not only to Alabama. but to Louisiana. Mississippi. Florida. and Arkansas. Now. why should not this bill apply to all those States ?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for concern that a bill applies to Alabama alone rather than other states affected by the original law.
- Look for comparing the proposal with an earlier law, including 'act of 1866'.
- Look for urging equal treatment across states named in the speech, like 'Louisiana', 'Mississippi', 'Florida', 'Arkansas'.

text: I thank the chairman. Again. I would like to encourage everybody with the few seconds I know I must have remaining. this is our chance in this House to fulfill the promise of 1964 and let the poor people of America put that roof over their head that they want.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for framing housing access as fulfilling the promise of 1964.
- Look for concern for low-income Americans like 'poor people of America'.
- Look for support for helping households secure housing like 'put that roof over their head'.

text: No. I do not think so. but whatever process Is the best for agriculture I think ought to be adopted. If the cyanamide process is the only process that can be utilized both for war and for peace. for powder and for fertilizers. I say candidly I propose to vote for that process. that is the process for me..
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for adopting whichever process best serves agriculture and practical needs.
- Look for willingness to back a technology with both military and civilian uses.
- Look for emphasis on fertilizer production and agricultural benefits like 'for fertilizers'.
- Look for a pragmatic, case-by-case stance rather than opposition based on the process itself.

text: Then that is superior. Thirdly. and really what bothers me the most. is that the Casey amendment does not cover an adequate number of crimes. including Federal crimes. It does not even cover the large number of heinous Federal crimes to which the amendment offered by the gentleman from Virginia would apply. is that correct?
label: R
explanation:
- Look for concern that legislation excludes too many offenses, including federal crimes.
- Look for emphasis on expanding coverage to heinous federal crimes.
- Look for criticism of the Casey amendment as inadequate in scope.

text: The case is very well stated. and laboriously stated. by the President and the Secretary of War. We do not regard it as a permanent standing army at all. The longest enlistment is for three years. and. of course. Congress will be here next winter to do as it pleases with the whole concern.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for a limited military commitment, emphasizing that enlistments are temporary rather than permanent.
- Look for confidence in Congress’s authority to revisit or change military policy.
- Look for deference to the President and Secretary of War when presenting the case for the measure.

text: The Senator is correct. This is the first time that controls such as those reported by the Committee on Foreign Relations have been so exercised. I think there is reason why we should have some control. I just happen to feel that the limit they have put on. in terms of total amount. is totally unrealistic.
label: R
explanation:
- Look for support for exercising controls over foreign relations.
- Look for criticism that a proposed funding limit is unrealistic.
- Look for a preference for some government oversight while objecting to the scale of a specific restriction.

text: I may say to the gentleman from New York that if he and the Members of the House will support the bill that the Reorganization Committee reported today. regardless of what is carried in the pending bill the President will have the power to put this agency under Civil Service.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for support for placing a federal agency under Civil Service.
- Look for a preference for congressional reorganization legislation to expand the President’s authority over agency staffing.

text: Let me say to the Senator that. according to figures which I have. furnished me by the Department. it could not possibly cost the Government more than $25.000.000 a year. and the statement made here the other day that it would cost the Government a hundred million dollars seems to me impossible of demonstration.
label: D
explanation:
- Look for challenging a substantially higher estimate of government spending.
- Look for using a specific annual cost figure to argue that a public program would be affordable, like 'more than $25.000.000 a year'.
- Look for disputing claims about fiscal impact as unsupported, like 'impossible of demonstration'.

text: Is the gentleman serious about that? If we had a Democratic President and a Democratic Secretary of the Treasury and a Democratic Postmaster General. would the gentleman stand on this floor and fight our own party and say our party is not competent to administer this fund. as he is now saying of the present majority party?
label: D
explanation:
- Look for criticism of claims that the current majority party is incompetent to administer a public fund.
- Look for a hypothetical about whether the same standard would apply under a different party's president and cabinet.
- Look for challenging partisan double standards with rhetorical questions like 'Is the gentleman serious about that?'.
